scenario: [LFST.7.1.3]: a tier's stream has its own `seq`, starting at 0. A single-tier session (one Trig asserted at t=0, one pump, one rule fire) is recorded by each runtime's own writer and read back, and the stream's first event atom, the assert's clock sample (`ClockAdvance`, recorded before its input, [LTIM.2.8.5]), carries seq 0. `StreamHeader`, `SchemaDef` and `Slot` carry no seq. Only the start is pinned: a recording carries a subset of the stream's events, so its later seqs skip the events the recorder does not write, and this vector says nothing about them. A live stream callback cannot pin the start: it is registered after load, so whatever the engine numbered before it is unobserved (RTIM.6.13d). The recording is the one view that starts at the stream's first atom. `expected_first_seq` is [RCTS.1.2.10]'s `rfcs_roundtrip` field for it. PATH PINNED: libds's `ds_rfcs_record_to` writer, read back through libds's reader (`pyds.atoms`) in runner.py `_run_rfcs_roundtrip` (the `seq` of the first atom after the `StreamHeader`, the `SchemaDef`s and their `Slot`s); the Mercury runtime's `ds.rfcs` `encode_stream`, read back through `decode_stream` in compiler/mercury/test/test_behave.m `rfcs_roundtrip_result` (`dsm_first_seq`, which `ds.rfcs` reads off the first event atom's body). A writer that numbered a stream from 1 fails here.
